correctness.rationale: For singular \(\kappa\), set \(\mu=\operatorname{cf}(\kappa)\) and choose a strictly increasing cofinal sequence \(\langle\kappa_i:i<\mu\rangle\). On level \(\kappa_j\), take the nodes on branches \(B_{\kappa_i}\) for \(i>j\). Each level then has size exactly \(\mu\); every pair of subsystem levels has comparable nodes on a later branch; predecessor coherence follows from tree order. Since \(\mu^+<\kappa\), the subsystem is narrow. Every positive fan node has cone bounded by its branch height, so no height-\(\kappa\) well-pruned subtree exists. These steps establish all quantifiers for every singular cardinal in ZFC.

value.rationale: The counterexample is a natural boundary theorem for a very recent structural result. It shows that ordinary narrowness, despite being strong enough at regular heights, is insufficient at every singular height, and it identifies \(\operatorname{cf}(\kappa)\) as the exact branch-family scale already in the canonical fan. This directly clarifies what any singular-height extension must control and is not a mere parameter substitution or finite recomputation.
